questions.question:
If A denotes 'addition'. B denotes 'multiplication', C denotes 'subtraction', and D denotes 'division', then what will be the value of the following equation?

(46 D 23) A 17 C 13 = ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50723751bca1df33fc1f030f78c1eac3344f2cdb432474cd432c6df783a12ab.png] 

 
 

 Alphabet
 A
 B
 C
 D
 
 

 Means
 +
 × 
 -
 ÷ 
 
 

The given expression : (46 D 23) A 17 C 13 = ?

After interchanging the symbols by mathematical operators the expression is as follows : (46 ÷ 23) + 17 - 13

= __**(46 ÷ 23)**__ + 17 - 13

= __**2 + 17**__ - 13

= __**19 - 13**__

= **6**

Hence, the correct answer is** "6".**

questions.question: Seven teachers Anil, Kamal, Ram, Sanjay, Aakash, Vivek and Rahul are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Sanjay is to the immediate right of Anil. Anil is third to the right of Rahul. Vivek is not the immediate neighbour of Aakash. Kamal is second to the right of Vivek. Who is second to the right of Anil?
questions.solution:

1. Sanjay is to the immediate right of Anil and Anil is third to the right of Rahul.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eef16660682fad717878b29c9132f7d60182f7184d4bbb0b9cc0de3767be2add.png]

3. Vivek is not an immediate neighbour of Aakash which means Aakash is sitting to the immediate left of Anil. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c788687813a5ec65509958891357bf294d29397a01cf5162dd4fca22ac45b012.png] 

4. There is only one place left for Ram. So, Ram will sit to the immediate right of Sanjay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2987728f0b893ee21d83ec3499d16d999391a0fc5c8a15e6834d6de2c5b8b9cc.png] 

Here, second to the right of Anil is **'**Ram**'.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option (3)".

questions.question:
Speed of six bikes T1, T2, T3, T4, T5 and T6 are compared. Speed of T6 is more than only three bikes. No two bikes have same speed. Speed of T4 is more than T2 but less than T6. Speed of T3 is not less than T5. Speed of T2 is not least. Speed of which bikes can be more than T4?

I. T3

II. T1
questions.solution:
**Given : **

 
• Speed of six bikes T1, T2, T3, T4, T5 and T6 are compared.
 
• No two bikes have same speed. 

**Explanation :**

1) Speed of T6 is more than only three bikes.

2) Speed of T4 is more than T2 but less than T6.

3) Speed of T2 is not least.

_ > _ > T6 > T4 > T2 > _

4) Speed of T3 is not less than T5.

As position of T5 is not known yet, therefore there are two possible positions for T5.

After positioning T5 and T3 only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e T1.

T3 > T1 / T5 > T6 > T4 > T2 > T1 / T5

Thus, according to the final arrangement Speed of three bikes i.e T3, T6 and either T1 or T5 is more than T4.

Therefore, 

I. T3 → It has more speed than T4.

II. T1 → It has more speed than T4.

Hence, **"Both I and II"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All A are G.

II. Some M are G.

**Conclusion:**

I. Some G are A.

II. Some G are M.

III. All M are A.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follows
Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90ab9041bf14f74e30b974cf5ab127357e2896c4c8d7f9902e649cd269784ef3.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some G are A → Follow (As all A are G. So, as whole A comes in G therefore, it is definitely true)

II. Some G are M → Follow (As some M are G. So, as some part of M is common with G therefore it is definitely true)

III. All M are A → Does not follow (As all A are G and some M are G. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Both conclusions I and II follows**".
